t: ff.145 Sugar, bones and crème brûlée
st: Food design against “the new smoking”: food

sec.p: Every week a new AI model is released with startling results (the latest is Gemini 3 and its 48.4% on Humanity's Next Exam). So, for a while now, I've argued that as automation grows, humans will have to take refuge in physiology, our natural substrate.
Speaking of bones. In Sugar Bones, Martí Guixé imagined sugar cubes with insoluble residue inside: fossils of our sugary consumption.

sec.t: ff.145.3 Blood-sugar spikes (and how to avoid them)
sec.p: In Glucose Revolution, Jessie Inchauspé argues that we're molecularly illiterate. We stop at calories and labels, when we should be focusing on the “ratios” between nutrients.

sec.t: ff.145.4 Food seriously harms your health
sec.p: This energy rollercoaster isn't your fault, though.
And so, back to Martí Guixé.

rel: ff.49 The pandemic of the 21st century
ff.35 I'm fine, I'm a Super Sapiens
